title: Capture the idea before it disappears
summary: Three hooks, a short video script, and two companion posts about keeping a useful content idea inbox.
assumptions: The intended audience is new creators juggling content with other work.
No platform or commercial offer was specified, so the drafts are platform-neutral and invite a practical action.

brief.source_idea: User note: I keep forgetting content ideas when I am out. I want to show people a simple idea inbox using phone notes: idea, who it helps, one concrete example.
brief.audience: New creators who capture ideas between other commitments
brief.goal: Help viewers save an idea with enough context to develop it later

selected_angle.title: Save the context, not just the topic
selected_angle.takeaway: Capture an idea, the person it helps, and one example while they are still clear.
selected_angle.reason: The user's three-field inbox supplies a small action viewers can try immediately.

assets.title: A three-line idea inbox
assets.content:
Ever opened a note that says 'content planning' and thought, 'What was I going to say?'

I keep forgetting content ideas when I'm out. So here's the phone-note version I'd use to hang on to the actual thought.

Three lines: the idea, who it helps, and one example.

Say the idea is a phone-note inbox. Who's it for? New creators thinking of posts between work and the commute. What could you show? One note with those three lines filled in.

That's something to come back to. You've got the point, the person you're talking to, and an example to start with.

Next time an idea hits, give future you all three lines.
assets.caption: 'What was I going to say?' Give future you a clue: the idea, who it's for, and one example.
assets.call_to_action: Next time an idea hits, give future you all three lines.
production_notes: Spoken length: roughly 110 words, or 45–55 seconds at 120–150 words per minute; check with a read-through.
Record a simple talking-head shot and optionally show the sample phone note; hide unrelated personal notes.
Optional on-screen text: Idea / Who it helps / One example.

assets.title: The note you can use later
assets.content:
Future you needs more than a two-word note.

A tiny template for the next idea that shows up while you're out:

Idea: I want to talk about ___.
Who it helps: This is for someone who ___.
Example: I could show them ___.

The last line is worth filling in. 'Content planning' can go in a dozen directions. One example gives you somewhere to start.

Copy the three lines into a phone note for your next idea.
assets.call_to_action: Copy the three lines into a phone note for your next idea.

assets.title: Revisit an old idea
assets.content:
This note definitely made sense when you wrote it.

Now it's just 'productivity video' staring back at you.

Before you try to turn it into a whole post, add the missing context: who it's for and one example you could show.

If the topic points to several different posts, choose the one with the clearest example. Leave the others in your inbox.

Open one old idea and finish this sentence: 'I could show this with…'
assets.call_to_action: Open one old idea and finish this sentence: 'I could show this with…'

review_notes: The personal statement about forgetting ideas comes from the user's note.
The drafts make no measured productivity, revenue, or audience-growth claims.
